ei.title: Don't Let Anger Be Your Boss
ei.subject: 공통영어1

fullPassage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry? One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents. Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem. However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life.

As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing. In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions. In your teen years, this part is still in development. The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity. At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are. You may also be more sensitive to unfairness. Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones. This significantly affects your mood. The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions.

It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you. Anger can sometimes be a useful tool. For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends. The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior. This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry. Rather, you should express it in a productive way. Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings. This can help you to better understand your anger.

You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense.

In some cases, the strategies mentioned above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically aggressive. Explore various strategies to discover what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind. You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one. By developing problem-solving skills, you will learn that there are many ways to solve a problem without getting angry.

Anger is an emotion that we all experience. By managing your anger properly, you can be the boss of your feelings, not the other way around. This is an important step in finding your true self and taking control of your life.

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ② slam → slamming: 'be동사(are) + V-ing'는 현재진행형이라 동사는 -ing 형태로 써야 해요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① suddenly — 'suddenly feeling angry(갑자기 화가 나는)'에서 동사 feeling을 꾸며 주는 부사로 올바릅니다.

✅ ② slam — 원래는 slamming입니다. 앞에 you're(=you are)가 있어서 'be + V-ing(현재진행형, ~하고 있다)' 형태가 돼야 해요. 그래서 slam이 아니라 slamming이 맞아요. ←정답

❌ ③ rolling — 'slamming doors or rolling your eyes'에서 앞의 slamming과 짝을 이루는 -ing 형태로 올바릅니다.

❌ ④ getting — 'are getting too upset(너무 화가 나고 있는)'에서 진행형으로 올바릅니다.
det.tip: be동사 + V-ing = 현재진행형 (지금 ~하고 있다)

det.korean: ① responsibly → responsible: be동사(is) 뒤에는 상태를 나타내는 형용사가 와야 해요(부사 X).

✅ ① responsibly — 원래는 responsible입니다. 'a part that is ___ for'에서 be동사 is 뒤에는 '책임이 있는'이라는 형용사 responsible이 와야 해요. responsibly(책임감 있게)는 부사라서 be동사 뒤에 못 와요. ←정답

❌ ② controlling — 'for solving problems and controlling your emotions'에서 앞의 solving과 짝을 이루는 동명사로 올바릅니다.

❌ ③ confused — 'feel confused(혼란스러움을 느끼다)'에서 감정을 나타내는 형용사로 올바릅니다.

❌ ④ sensitive — 'be more sensitive to(~에 더 민감하다)'에서 형용사로 올바릅니다.
det.tip: be동사 + 형용사(보어): is responsible (부사 responsibly 아님)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ③ that → what: 앞에 꾸밈 받을 명사(선행사)가 없으면 '~하는 것'이라는 관계대명사 what을 써야 해요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① mentioned — 'the strategies mentioned above(위에서 언급된 전략들)'에서 명사를 뒤에서 꾸미는 과거분사로 올바릅니다.

❌ ② becoming — 'find yourself becoming ~(~해지는 자신을 발견하다)'에서 find + 목적어 + 현재분사(-ing) 형태로 올바릅니다.

✅ ③ that — 원래는 what입니다. 'discover ___ is best for you'에서 앞에 꾸밈 받을 명사가 없어요. 이럴 때는 '~하는 것'이라는 뜻을 스스로 담은 관계대명사 what을 써요. that은 앞에 명사(선행사)가 있어야 해서 틀려요. ←정답

det.tip: 선행사 없이 '~하는 것' = 관계대명사 what (that과 구별)

questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~④ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: ② worsen → resolve: 열린 대화는 갈등을 '해결'하는 것이므로 worsen(악화시키다)은 반대예요.
det.analysis:
❌ ① useful — 'Anger can sometimes be a useful tool(분노는 때때로 유용한 도구가 될 수 있다)'. 뒤에 좋은 예가 이어지므로 적절합니다.

✅ ② worsen — 원래는 resolve입니다. '열리고 솔직한 대화가 친구 사이 갈등을 ___한다'인데, 대화는 갈등을 '해결(resolve)'하는 거예요. worsen(악화시키다)은 정반대라 틀려요. ←정답

❌ ③ manage — 'manage your anger(분노를 관리하다)'. 분노를 다스린다는 문맥에 적절합니다.

❌ ④ aggressive — 'aggressive or violent behavior(공격적이거나 폭력적인 행동)'. 관리하지 않으면 나타날 행동이라 적절합니다.
det.tip: resolve a conflict = 갈등을 해결하다 (↔ worsen 악화)

You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way. Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice. The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger. It is possible to recognize those signs in advance. They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists. When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger. For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense.

In some cases, the strategies mentioned above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation. Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically aggressive. Explore various strategies to discover what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind. You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one. By developing problem-solving skills, you will learn that there are many ways to solve a problem without getting angry.

questions.passage:
Do you ever find yourself suddenly feeling angry?  One moment you're fine, and the next moment you're slamming doors or rolling your eyes at your parents.  Some people may think you just have a bad attitude or are getting too upset about a small problem.  However, these feelings don't simply come from stress about everyday life. 

As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing.  In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions.  In your teen years, this part is still in development.  The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity.  At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are.  You may also be more sensitive to unfairness.  Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones.  This significantly affects your mood.  The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions. 

It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you.  Anger can sometimes be a useful tool.  For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends.  The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior.  This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry.  Rather, you should express it in a productive way.  Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings.  This can help you to better understand your anger. 

You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way.

det.korean: intensify → intensifies: 주어의 핵심이 단수(combination)라서 동사에 -s를 붙여야 해요.
det.analysis:
밑줄이 있는 문장은 'The combination of these factors ___ your strong emotions(이런 요인들의 결합이 너의 강한 감정을 ___한다)'예요.

① 동사 앞의 진짜 주어를 찾아야 해요. 주어는 'The combination(그 결합)'이고, 'of these factors(이런 요인들의)'는 주어를 꾸미는 부분이라 동사 수와 상관없어요.

② combination은 단수라서, 현재형 동사에는 -s를 붙여요. 그래서 intensify가 아니라 intensifies가 맞아요.

③ 이렇게 of 뒤의 복수 명사(factors)에 속지 않고, 진짜 주어(combination)에 맞춰 동사를 쓰는 것이 핵심이에요.
det.tip: 주어 = combination(단수) → 동사 intensifies (of factors에 속지 말기)

As a teen, you may feel like an adult, but your brain is still growing.  In your brain, there is a part that is responsible for solving problems and controlling your emotions.  In your teen years, this part is still in development.  The changes in your brain lead you toward independence, social engagement, and creativity.  At the same time, however, you may feel confused about who you are.  You may also be more sensitive to unfairness.  Furthermore, your body is flowing with hormones.  This significantly affects your mood.  The combination of these factors intensifies your strong emotions. 

It is natural to feel angry from time to time; it doesn't mean there is something wrong with you.  Anger can sometimes be a useful tool.  For example, an angry but open conversation can resolve a conflict between friends.  The important thing is to manage your anger so that it does not turn into aggressive or violent behavior.  This does not mean that you should stop yourself from feeling angry.  Rather, you should express it in a productive way.  Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings.  This can help you to better understand your anger. 

You need to learn how to deal with anger in a socially appropriate way.  Remember: anger is a feeling, but behavior is a choice.  The first step is recognizing the physical signs of anger.  It is possible to recognize those signs in advance.  They include an increased heart rate, a flushed face, and the clenching of your fists.  When these things happen, take action to reduce your anger.  For example, you could try taking a break to organize your thoughts or ending a conversation before it gets too intense. 

In some cases, the strategies mentioned above may not be enough, so you may need to find proper coping skills for your personal situation.  Without the right coping skills, you may find yourself becoming verbally or even physically aggressive.  Explore various strategies to discover what is best for you, such as taking a walk, drawing a picture, or writing down things that come to your mind.  You can also try to find possible solutions to a problem and then compare the advantages and disadvantages of each one.  By developing problem-solving skills, you will learn that there are many ways to solve a problem without getting angry.

questions.stem:
다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.
"분노는 우리 모두가 경험하는 감정이다."
[조건] (1) all, an, anger, emotion, experience, is, that, we 를 모두 사용 (2) 8단어 (3) 영어로 쓸 것

det.korean: anger is an emotion that we all experience (분노는 우리 모두가 경험하는 감정이다)
det.analysis:
명사를 뒤에서 문장으로 꾸며 주는 관계대명사 문제예요.

① '분노는 ~감정이다'의 뼈대는 anger is an emotion이에요.

② '우리 모두가 경험하는'이 앞의 emotion을 꾸며 줘요. 이렇게 명사를 꾸미는 문장은 관계대명사 that으로 이어요. 'emotion that ~(~하는 감정)'.

③ '우리 모두가 경험하는'은 we all experience로 써요. experience의 목적어가 앞의 emotion이라서 that 뒤에는 목적어 없이 we all experience만 와요.

전부 이으면 anger is an emotion that we all experience, 총 8단어예요.
det.tip: 명사 + that + 주어 + 동사 = ~하는 (명사) [목적격 관계대명사]

다음 우리말에 맞도록 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.
"너의 화난 감정에 대해 스스로에게 몇 가지 질문을 해 보라."

[ about / angry / Ask / feelings / questions / some / your / yourself ] (8단어) (영어로)

det.korean: 정답: Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings (너의 화난 감정에 대해 스스로에게 몇 가지 질문을 해 보라)
det.analysis:
명령문(~해 보라)이라 동사로 시작하는 어순 배열이에요.

① '~해 보라'는 명령문이라 동사원형 Ask로 시작해요. 'Ask yourself(스스로에게 물어보라)'가 돼요.

② '몇 가지 질문을'은 some questions예요.

③ '너의 화난 감정에 대해'는 about your angry feelings예요. about(~에 대해) + your(너의) + angry(화난) + feelings(감정).

전부 이으면 Ask yourself some questions about your angry feelings, 총 8단어예요.

다음 우리말에 맞도록 [조건]에 따라 영작하시오.
"너는 네가 누구인지에 대해 혼란스러움을 느낄 수도 있다."
[조건] (1) about, are, confused, feel, may, who, you, you 를 모두 사용 (2) 8단어 (3) 영어로 쓸 것

det.korean: you may feel confused about who you are (너는 네가 누구인지에 대해 혼란스러움을 느낄 수도 있다)
det.analysis:
감정 형용사와 '간접의문문'을 함께 쓰는 문제예요.

① '느낄 수도 있다'는 '~할 수도 있다'의 may와 '느끼다'의 feel을 합쳐 you may feel로 시작해요.

② '혼란스러움을'은 감정을 나타내는 형용사 confused를 써요. 'feel confused(혼란스러움을 느끼다)'.

③ '네가 누구인지에 대해'는 about + 간접의문문이에요. 간접의문문은 '의문사 + 주어 + 동사' 순서라서 who you are(누구 + 너는 + 이다)로 써요.

전부 이으면 you may feel confused about who you are, 총 8단어예요.
det.tip: 간접의문문 = 의문사 + 주어 + 동사 (who you are, who are you 아님)
